card.line: Iconium was a large, rich city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preached, many believed, and enemies drove them out, and where new believers were later strengthened.

moments.title: Driven to Iconium
moments.text: After Jews stirred up trouble and drove Paul and Barnabas out of their district, they shook the dust off their feet and went to Iconium. The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.

moments.title: Preaching in the synagogue
moments.text: Paul and Barnabas went into the Jewish synagogue and spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed. They stayed a long time and spoke boldly, and the Lord affirmed His message with signs and wonders.

moments.title: Stoned in Lystra
moments.text: Some Jews from Antioch and Iconium won over the crowds in Lystra. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead, but he got up and went back in.

moments.title: Encouraging the disciples
moments.text: On the way back, Paul and Barnabas returned to Iconium and other cities. They strengthened the disciples, told them to keep believing, and appointed elders in each church.

moments.title: Timothy's good name
moments.text: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of Timothy, a disciple Paul wanted to take along with him.
